tools.name: Scam Guard
tools.what: Checks submitted texts, links, numbers or images for signs of scams such as phishing, fake shipping alerts, dating and job scams, and recommends actions.

tools.name: StopScam
tools.what: Gives a plain-language read of a suspicious text, link, screenshot or file, with warning signs and a practical next step.

tools.name: AI Scam Checker
tools.what: Rates a pasted message, screenshot, link, QR code or described call as safe, suspicious or dangerous, with an explanation and what to do next.

tools.name: Scam Mirror
tools.what: Reviews up to five related items from one suspicious case and combines visible evidence, known scam patterns and public-source signals into a probabilistic risk assessment.
tools.gap: Its own site states the result is not identity verification, legal advice, financial advice or proof of criminal intent.

tools.name: Safe House Project education
tools.what: Publishes articles and trainings on how traffickers use social media and gaming platforms to groom and recruit children, including fake identities and isolation.
tools.gap: Offers education, training and a reporting tool (Simply Report) rather than a personalised check of an individual situation.

tools.name: Not For Sale glossary and articles
tools.what: Publishes a glossary and articles explaining trafficking terms including coercion, isolation, online recruitment and digital grooming.
tools.gap: Provides reference education rather than a personalised check of an individual situation.

tools.name: Bridging Freedom Get the Facts
tools.what: Publishes resource pages and downloadable guides on child sex trafficking, online safety for children and recognising the signs.
tools.gap: Provides downloadable guides for parents and children rather than a personalised check of an individual situation.
